tasks.title: bs results check: the gate's paperwork before hand-back, per role
tasks.summary: Factory-level. A read-only `bs results check <task-id> --as <coder|tester|grader|gate>` runs checkPaperwork with the role's stage set; gate mode takes the `gate run` line verbatim, parses its files with the gate's own intake, dry-runs its judge closes and runs no check command.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix. Add `bs results check <task-id> --as <coder|tester|grader|gate>` to factory/orchestrator/src/cli.ts and its entry to usage.ts COMMANDS. It is the preflight that workers run before hand-back and the wave-runner runs before `gate run`. It calls task-1's `checkPaperwork` with `as` set and adds no validation logic of its own. The task id is positional, as in `gate run`. Role modes (coder, tester, grader) take the flags a worker's brief line carries: `--result <file>` (coder, tester), `--grader <file>` (grader), `--agent <role> --provider <name> --model-tier <tier> [--input-tokens <n> --output-tokens <n>]` stamped through results.ts `stampResultEnvelope` exactly as the `gate run` arm does (cli.ts:3823-3833), `--worktree <dir>` (required for coder), `--base <ref>`, `--plan <plan.json>` (required for tester, read for `ui_affecting` the way `gate run` reads it), `--artifacts-dir <dir>`, and the events-dir and session flags. A role mode refuses every gate-only flag (`--checks`, `--run-all`, `--evidence`, `--found-by`, `--found-by-provider`, `--findings`, `--no-findings`, `--uiux-visual`, `--lessons`) with a usage error naming `--as gate`. Gate mode accepts the `gate run` line verbatim: every flag usage.ts lists for `gate run`, with the same required flags. It reads every file on that line with the gate's own intake functions: `readChecksFile` for `--checks` (cli.ts:352; parsed, never run), `readFindingsInputFile` (cli.ts:312), `evidenceSources` and `mintFromEvidence` (cli.ts:1019, 1061), `mintFromUiuxVisual` (cli.ts:1084), `parseLessons`, and the `--grader` file. It never spawns a check. Judge-close dry run: `gate run` closes the judge turns its own line hands in before the gate's judges stage (cli.ts:3874-3901, and `--no-findings` at cli.ts:3909-3921), so a read-only preflight must know which closes that line would make and whether each would succeed. Extract the selection of those closes (the same closeKey rule: once per role and kind, only for an unreported turn of that role and kind) into one helper in cli.ts that both arms call. Extract from judges.ts `recordJudgeReport` (judges.ts:921) everything it checks before it appends (the kind check, turn selection, artifact freshness, `readJudgeArtifact`) into a new exported `checkJudgeReport(input, turns, opts)` that throws the same JudgeError codes and appends nothing; `recordJudgeReport` keeps its declaration and calls it. results check runs `checkJudgeReport` for each selected close: a throw is a blocked problem under its own code, and each close that would succeed is passed to checkPaperwork as `alsoReported`. Output, on stdout, one JSON document: `{outcome: 'pass' | 'blocked', reason?, as, task_id, artifact_home, problems, skipped, not_run, verdicts?, warnings}`. `not_run` names the gate stages a preflight never evaluates (`tests`, `coverage-evidence`, `findings`, `budget`). `artifact_home` is the absolute directory the artifact stage resolved, so a worker can see it is the one the gate will read. Exit 0 only on pass and 1 on blocked. A usage error or refusal exits 1 through the CLI's existing top-level error document `{error: {code, message, details}}` (cli.ts:5403-5420); there is no other exit code. An intake failure on a file the caller handed in is a blocked problem with a named reason, never a stack trace: `result-unreadable` (missing file, invalid JSON), `results.not-an-object`, `results.agent-wrote-owned-field`, `results.partial-token-count`, `results.invalid-token-count`, `artifacts.missing-task-id`, `artifacts.unsafe-task-id`, and any other SmithError or JudgeError code an intake function throws. A complete result document (no `--agent`) whose `task_id` differs from the positional id adds a `warnings` entry and does not block, as in the gate, which checks artifacts against its own task id (gate.ts:1228-1231). It writes nothing: no event, no result file, no judge-turn close. `bs uiux check` is unchanged; usage.ts says `results check --as gate` includes the uiux stage.

tasks.title: The gate records sleep evidence on a failed test run
tasks.summary: Factory-level. Each gate check records wall-clock and monotonic time, their gap, and the load average; a failed check whose own clock gap shows the machine slept stays blocked as tests-failed and is classified execution.env-failure. Load is evidence only. Nothing is re-run.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix. In factory/orchestrator/src/testgate.ts, measure around each check command: wall-clock ms, monotonic ms, their gap, the 1-minute load average at start and at end, and the CPU count. Put them on each CheckResult as an optional `environment` object that `run` always sets (optional on the type so integration.ts and other constructors compile unchanged). The clock and load sources are injectable through RunOptions and GateInput, with today's real sources as the default. Export a pure classifier and one named constant, `SLEEP_GAP_MS = 30_000`. The classifier fires on the clock gap only: `clock_gap_ms >= SLEEP_GAP_MS`. Node's monotonic clock (`process.hrtime`, libuv's uv_hrtime) does not advance while the machine is suspended on the platforms the factory runs on (macOS `mach_absolute_time`, Linux `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), while the wall clock does, so the gap measures time asleep; a check cannot put the machine to sleep, so a failing suite cannot cause its own classification. 30 s is far above NTP slew and below any real suspend worth naming; the constant's comment says so and names its source. On a platform whose monotonic clock counts suspend, the gap reads about 0 and the classifier never fires, which fails safe as a plain tests-failed block. Load is recorded as evidence only and never classifies: a full suite raises the 1-minute load average itself, so a load threshold would label real failures as environment failures. In gate.ts, when the test stage fails, run the classifier over each failed check's own evidence; a gap on a check that passed never classifies another check's failure. When it fires, the `testgate-result` payload, the `gate-outcome` payload and the returned blocked GateOutcome each carry `error_class: 'execution.env-failure'` and the failed check's evidence. The outcome stays `blocked`, the reason stays `tests-failed`, nothing is re-run, and the gate finalizes exactly as for any other tests-failed block. A run that passes is never classified, whatever its evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every CheckResult from `run` carries `environment: {wall_ms, monotonic_ms, clock_gap_ms, load_1m_start, load_1m_end, cpus}`; a test in test/testgate.test.ts with an injected clock and load source pins each value exactly.

Classifier boundary tests: a clock gap of `SLEEP_GAP_MS - 1` does not fire and one of `SLEEP_GAP_MS` does; a load per CPU of 100 at start and at end with a gap of 0 does not fire. `SLEEP_GAP_MS` is exported, named, and commented with the source of its value; no load threshold exists.

test/gateEnvEvidence.test.ts: a failing check whose injected gap is at least `SLEEP_GAP_MS` yields outcome `blocked`, reason `tests-failed`, and `error_class: 'execution.env-failure'` plus the evidence on the `testgate-result` payload, the `gate-outcome` payload and the returned GateOutcome. A failing check with a gap of 0 under very high injected load yields the same block with no `error_class`. A passing check with a gap above the threshold passes with no `error_class`. A run where check A passes with a gap above the threshold and check B fails with a gap of 0 is blocked with no `error_class`.

Each check command runs exactly once per gate call in the classified case: the fixture command appends one line to a counter file per run, and after the gate returns the file holds one line per check.
Every existing assertion in test/testgate.test.ts, test/gate.test.ts and test/heavyLock.test.ts passes unchanged; `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` and every other timeout are unchanged.
Production callers (cli.ts `gate run`, integration.ts, queue.ts) pass no source and get the real ones; no file outside this task's claims changes.

A problem the worker cannot fix in its own output (a flag its brief got wrong, an environment problem) is reported in `notes` as it stands, never worked around. A worker whose brief carries no such line says so in `notes`. bs-grader.md adds: the preflight checks the grader file's shape only; a well-formed fail verdict exits 0 and shows in `verdicts.grader`; the grader fixes shape (where the verdict sits, missing criterion fields, the round number) and never changes a verdict, a criterion's status or its evidence to get a clean preflight. It raises no finding against the coder, is not bounced to the coder, and the wave-runner does not re-run the gate on its own: whether and when to re-gate stays the epic session's decision, and a second env-classified block for the same task at the same HEAD goes to the operator. Steps 2-10 keep their numbers; dispatch.md is not edited. tasks.title: The gate records sleep evidence on a failed test run
tasks.summary: Factory-level. Each gate check records wall-clock and monotonic time over its own process, their gap, and the load average; a failed check whose own clock gap shows the machine slept stays blocked as tests-failed and is classified execution.env-failure. The heavy-lock wait is outside the window, a lock-wait timeout never classifies, load is evidence only, and nothing is re-run.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix. In factory/orchestrator/src/testgate.ts, measure each check command: wall-clock ms, monotonic ms, their gap, the 1-minute load average at start and at end, and the CPU count. Put them beside the check results, never inside CheckResult (finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-8de89739): test/testgate.test.ts:87-89 pins a passing check's CheckResult with an exact `toEqual`, and AC3 keeps that assertion unchanged. RunResult gains an optional `environment` array that `run` always sets: one entry per entry of `results`, in the same order, each `{name, window: 'command' | 'none', wall_ms, monotonic_ms, clock_gap_ms, load_1m_start, load_1m_end, cpus}`. It is index-aligned and carries the check's name rather than being keyed by name, because nothing makes check names in a checks file unique (cli.ts `readChecksFile`). CheckResult's declaration does not change, so integration.ts, which maps `results` into its own list, and every other CheckResult constructor and assertion are untouched; `runCumulative` returns `run`'s RunResult and so carries the array too. The gate's `testgate-result` payload carries the array as `environment`, beside `pass` and `results` (gate.ts `runGate`, the `emit('testgate-result', ...)` call at gate.ts:1459-1465); event.schema.json leaves a payload's shape open, so no schema changes. Where the window sits (finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-b1e1257b): it brackets the check's own process and nothing else. It opens immediately before `runOne` spawns the command and closes when that process closes, so the evidence measures the check, not the queue. For a heavy check (`isHeavyCheck`, testgate.ts:39-47, run through `runHeavy`, testgate.ts:326-360 at 99e7fe64) that is inside the `withHeavyLock` callback, after the lease is held: the lock wait stays in `lock_wait_ms`, measured as today, and never enters `clock_gap_ms`. A check whose lock wait timed out (`runHeavy`'s catch, `reason: 'heavy.wait-timeout'`) spawned no command, so its `environment` entry has `window: 'none'`, zero `wall_ms`, `monotonic_ms` and `clock_gap_ms`, one load sample taken when the wait ended as both `load_1m_start` and `load_1m_end`, and `cpus`; it never classifies, and its block stays `tests-failed` with its own `reason: heavy.wait-timeout` and no `error_class`. Every other entry has `window: 'command'`. The clock and load sources are injectable through RunOptions and GateInput, with today's real sources as the default; GateInput gains no lock option. Export a pure classifier and one named constant, `SLEEP_GAP_MS = 30_000`. The classifier fires on a `window: 'command'` entry whose clock gap is at least the constant: `clock_gap_ms >= SLEEP_GAP_MS`. Load is recorded as evidence only and never classifies: a full suite raises the 1-minute load average itself, so a load threshold would label real failures as environment failures. In gate.ts, when the test stage fails, run the classifier over each failed check's own `environment` entry; a gap on a check that passed never classifies another check's failure. The outcome stays `blocked`, the reason stays `tests-failed`, nothing is re-run, and the gate finalizes exactly as for any other tests-failed block. A run that passes is never classified, whatever its evidence. tasks.title: The gate records sleep evidence on a failed test run
tasks.summary: Factory-level. Each gate check records wall-clock and monotonic time over its own process, their gap, and the load average; a failed check whose own clock gap shows the machine slept stays blocked as tests-failed and is classified execution.env-failure. The heavy-lock wait is outside the window, a lock-wait timeout never classifies, load is evidence only, and nothing is re-run.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix. In factory/orchestrator/src/testgate.ts, measure each check command: wall-clock ms, monotonic ms, their gap, the 1-minute load average at start and at end, and the CPU count. Put them beside the check results, never inside CheckResult (finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-8de89739): test/testgate.test.ts:87-89 pins a passing check's CheckResult with an exact `toEqual`, and AC3 keeps that assertion unchanged. RunResult gains an optional `environment` array that `run` always sets: one entry per entry of `results`, in the same order, each `{name, window: 'command' | 'none', wall_ms, monotonic_ms, clock_gap_ms, load_1m_start, load_1m_end, cpus}`. It is index-aligned and carries the check's name rather than being keyed by name, because nothing makes check names in a checks file unique (cli.ts `readChecksFile`). CheckResult's declaration does not change, so integration.ts, which maps `results` into its own list, and every other CheckResult constructor and assertion are untouched; `runCumulative` returns `run`'s RunResult and so carries the array too. The gate's `testgate-result` payload carries the array as `environment`, beside `pass` and `results` (gate.ts `runGate`, the `emit('testgate-result', ...)` call at gate.ts:1459-1465); event.schema.json leaves a payload's shape open, so no schema changes. Where the window sits (finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-b1e1257b): it brackets the check's own process and nothing else. It opens immediately before `runOne` spawns the command and closes when that process closes, so the evidence measures the check, not the queue. For a heavy check (`isHeavyCheck`, testgate.ts:39-47, run through `runHeavy`, testgate.ts:326-360 at 99e7fe64) that is inside the `withHeavyLock` callback, after the lease is held: the lock wait stays in `lock_wait_ms`, measured as today, and never enters `clock_gap_ms`. A check whose lock wait timed out (`runHeavy`'s catch, `reason: 'heavy.wait-timeout'`) spawned no command, so its `environment` entry has `window: 'none'`, zero `wall_ms`, `monotonic_ms` and `clock_gap_ms`, one load sample taken when the wait ended as both `load_1m_start` and `load_1m_end`, and `cpus`; it never classifies, and its block stays `tests-failed` with its own `reason: heavy.wait-timeout` and no `error_class`. Every other entry has `window: 'command'`. The clock and load sources are injectable through RunOptions and GateInput, with today's real sources as the default; GateInput gains no lock option. Export a pure classifier and one named constant, `SLEEP_GAP_MS = 30_000`. The classifier fires on a `window: 'command'` entry whose clock gap is at least the constant: `clock_gap_ms >= SLEEP_GAP_MS`. Node's monotonic clock (`process.hrtime`, libuv's uv_hrtime) does not advance while the machine is suspended on the platforms the factory runs on (macOS `mach_absolute_time`, Linux `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), while the wall clock does, so the gap measures time asleep; a check cannot put the machine to sleep, so a failing suite cannot cause its own classification. 30 s is far above NTP slew and below any real suspend worth naming; the constant's comment says so and names its source. On a platform whose monotonic clock counts suspend, the gap reads about 0 and the classifier never fires, which fails safe as a plain tests-failed block. Load is recorded as evidence only and never classifies: a full suite raises the 1-minute load average itself, so a load threshold would label real failures as environment failures. In gate.ts, when the test stage fails, run the classifier over each failed check's own `environment` entry; a gap on a check that passed never classifies another check's failure. When it fires, the `testgate-result` payload, the `gate-outcome` payload and the returned blocked GateOutcome each carry `error_class: 'execution.env-failure'` and the failed check's evidence. The outcome stays `blocked`, the reason stays `tests-failed`, nothing is re-run, and the gate finalizes exactly as for any other tests-failed block. A run that passes is never classified, whatever its evidence. Tests never take the machine's heavy lock: test/setup.ts already points BS_HEAVY_LOCK_DIR at a per-file temp directory (setup.ts:40-48); on top of that, test/gateEnvEvidence.test.ts marks its checks `heavy: false` (or gives them non-heavy names), and a test/testgate.test.ts case about a heavy check passes `heavyLock: {lockDir}` with a `mkdtemp` directory, as test/heavyLock.test.ts does. The `error_class` on the gate-outcome is what task-6 counts toward lesson recurrence (AC10); criterion 9 pins that the field this task writes is the field task-6 reads. test/paperwork.test.ts (task-1, merged) pins the gate lineage in inline snapshots; its `lineageOf` helper renders a testgate-result payload with the `environment` value replaced by a placeholder that keeps the key and the entry count (the values are clock- and load-dependent), and no other line or snapshot in that file changes.
acceptance_criteria: Every RunResult from `run` carries `environment`, one entry per check result in the same order, each `{name, window, wall_ms, monotonic_ms, clock_gap_ms, load_1m_start, load_1m_end, cpus}`, and no CheckResult gains a field; a test in test/testgate.test.ts with an injected clock and load source pins each value exactly on a `window: 'command'` entry, and a run of two checks with the same name gets two entries in order (finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-8de89739).

Classifier boundary tests: a clock gap of `SLEEP_GAP_MS - 1` does not fire and one of `SLEEP_GAP_MS` does; a load per CPU of 100 at start and at end with a gap of 0 does not fire; a `window: 'none'` entry never fires, whatever its fields. `SLEEP_GAP_MS` is exported, named, and commented with the source of its value; no load threshold exists.

test/gateEnvEvidence.test.ts: a failing check whose injected gap is at least `SLEEP_GAP_MS` yields outcome `blocked`, reason `tests-failed`, and `error_class: 'execution.env-failure'` plus the evidence on the `testgate-result` payload, the `gate-outcome` payload and the returned GateOutcome. A failing check with a gap of 0 under very high injected load yields the same block with no `error_class`. A passing check with a gap above the threshold passes with no `error_class`. A run where check A passes with a gap above the threshold and check B fails with a gap of 0 is blocked with no `error_class`.

Each check command runs exactly once per gate call in the classified case: the fixture command appends one line to a counter file per run, and after the gate returns the file holds one line per check.

Window placement (finding b1e1257b): a test/testgate.test.ts case runs a heavy check on a `mkdtemp` lockDir that a stub holder keeps for a few polls (any mechanism the injectable `heavyLock` options allow, e.g. `isPidAlive`), with the injected clock and the liveness probe writing to one ordered log: every clock read comes after the last liveness probe, `lock_wait_ms` is greater than 0, and `clock_gap_ms` is exactly the injected gap. A second case whose holder outlives `maxWaitMs` returns a check result with `reason: 'heavy.wait-timeout'` whose `environment` entry has `window: 'none'`, zero clock fields and one load sample in both load fields, and spawns nothing (a marker command leaves no marker).

Every existing assertion in test/testgate.test.ts, test/gate.test.ts and test/heavyLock.test.ts passes unchanged, the exact `toEqual` at test/testgate.test.ts:87-89 included, because CheckResult gains no field (finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-8de89739); `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` and every other timeout are unchanged.

Production callers (cli.ts `gate run`, integration.ts, queue.ts) pass no source and get the real ones; heavyRun.ts and queue.ts, which import `heavyChildEnv`, are untouched and `heavyChildEnv` keeps its declaration; no file outside this task's claims changes.

No test in this task takes the machine's heavy lock: every lock a new test takes lives under a `mkdtemp` directory (test/setup.ts's per-file BS_HEAVY_LOCK_DIR, or an explicit `heavyLock.lockDir`), and test/gateEnvEvidence.test.ts's checks are not heavy (finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-b1e1257b).

Counted by the recurrence rule (AC10, finding a8609c17): in test/gateEnvEvidence.test.ts, after a classified block on one task and an unclassified tests-failed block on a second, lessonEvents.ts `readRecurrenceEvents` over the test's events directory and lessonRecurrence.ts `errorClassCounts` (task-6) count the first task under `execution.env-failure` and not under `execution.test-failure`, and the second under `execution.test-failure`.
